items.headline: Marvell to acquire Lumentum in all-stock AI connectivity deal
items.summary: Marvell Technology agreed to buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal, giving Lumentum shareholders 4.5 Marvell shares each to combine electrical and optical technologies for AI networking. The deal, expected to close in the first half of 2028, marks one of the largest AI infrastructure bets of 2026.

items.headline: OpenAI signs sweeping AI deals with Abu Dhabi's ADNOC and G42
items.summary: OpenAI inked agreements with ADNOC, G42, Mubadala and Inception42 to deploy frontier AI across energy, investment analysis, government and education. The pacts include translating Abu Dhabi government policies into machine-readable form and a five-year frontier AI adoption deal.

items.headline: Anthropic files amended IPO prospectus revealing financials
items.summary: Anthropic released an amended S-1 for its upcoming IPO, disclosing it generated $33.24 billion and detailing massive compute commitments. The filing sharpens scrutiny of investor appetite for loss-making AI developers ahead of one of the biggest IPOs in history.

items.headline: Tempus wins two FDA clearances for AI cardiology tools
items.summary: Tempus received two 510(k) clearances from the FDA for its ECG-PH and ECG-MR non-invasive AI cardiology products, expanding its diagnostic footprint. The company also cleared regulatory review of its pending acquisition of Personalis.

items.headline: Howard Marks says AI stumbles have boosted market skepticism
items.summary: Oaktree Capital co-chair Howard Marks told Bloomberg TV that recent AI-related market stumbles have punctured the sector's aura of infallibility. His comments reflect growing investor caution amid the AI boom's rising valuations.

items.headline: Anthropic warns its AI could pose existential risks to humanity
items.summary: Anthropic warned its AI could 'pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity' without appropriate safeguards, oversight and security. The dire self-assessment stands out even among the industry's many warnings as the company courts IPO investors.

items.headline: NHS trusts leave AI tools unused despite touted benefits
items.summary: The Guardian reported that AI technology said to be benefiting the NHS is unused or little used by 29 trusts. The findings raise questions about the gap between AI hype and real-world healthcare adoption.

items.headline: Fortune: It might be OK that the AI boom hit a wall
items.summary: Fortune argued that the AI boom's recent Wall Street setbacks may be healthy, tempering unsustainable expectations. The analysis comes amid rising bond yields and political backlash against data center spending.

items.headline: The Atlantic probes record AI data center spending
items.summary: The Atlantic examined how the five largest AI-data-center companies are on track to spend $900 billion in 2026 and its outsized role in the economy. The piece ties the spending boom to political claims about economic strength ahead of the midterms.

items.headline: Nature paper argues AI needs meaningful versioning
items.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence paper by Mavroudis, Ristea, Morlock and colleagues makes the case for meaningful versioning of AI systems. The research addresses reproducibility and accountability gaps as models rapidly evolve.

items.headline: AI concerns move to the center of US midterm campaigns
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that AI has become a major midterm election issue, with candidates clashing over regulation, data centers, jobs and safety. A Democratic Congress could bring a more aggressive regulatory approach to the sector.

items.headline: AI talent war spreads to Wall Street quant firms
items.summary: Quantitative trading firms are competing with AI labs for top scientists, with first-year compensation for some PhDs reaching $800,000. Firms are deploying fellowships, university sponsorships and recruiting events to win talent.

items.headline: China's embodied AI firms raise $13 billion in H1 2026
items.summary: Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan ($13 billion) across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times the prior year. The surge reflects a race to pair robot bodies with capable AI 'brains.'

items.headline: Anthropic updates Usage Policy with model-welfare provisions
items.summary: Anthropic updated its Usage Policy, including a prohibition on sustained, needless abusive or cruel behavior toward its Claude models. The company said it will keep revising the policy as Claude's capabilities and risks evolve.

items.headline: Anthropic's S-1 details $389.9 billion compute commitments
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus revealed at least $389.9 billion in compute commitments, including $44.9 billion with Microsoft between November 2026 and May 2033. The filing exposes deep dependencies on Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Broadcom for computing power.

items.headline: Anthropic reveals $80.7 billion net loss amid explosive growth
items.summary: Anthropic's net loss widened to $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, largely from the rising fair value of convertible bonds, on revenue of about $16.3 billion. Some investors are weighing a lower valuation of around $1.5 trillion following the disclosures.

items.headline: Meta AI director Rohit Patel leaves to launch startup
items.summary: Meta AI director Rohit Patel departed to build a startup targeting Microsoft Office and Google Workspace as the platform for enterprise work. His venture enters a crowded field where OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google are racing to own workplace AI.

items.headline: Anthropic unveils Claude Duet proactive AI agent app
items.summary: Anthropic unveiled Claude Duet, a standalone AI agent app designed to act as a proactive assistant for professionals and small-business owners. The launch intensifies competition with OpenAI and Meta in the agentic AI workspace race.

items.headline: Otter.ai raises $320 million to expand enterprise business
items.summary: Otter.ai secured $320 million in non-equity financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund to grow its enterprise offerings. The deal highlights alternative financing structures gaining traction among AI companies.
